meta.title: The Delay Line
meta.subtitle: Inside the interpolation buffer: an irregular write pointer, a servo-driven read pointer, and the guess it makes when the waypoints run out

views.label: The write side is irregular
views.note: Packets land whenever the wire delivers them. Each one drops into a tick-stamped slot.

views.label: How deep the buffer sits
views.note: The larger of the configured window and the measured jitter wins, so a bad link deepens the buffer for you.

views.label: The read pointer is a servo
views.note: It never jumps for small errors. It runs a bit fast or a bit slow until the error is gone.

views.label: When it runs out of waypoints
views.note: With nothing newer to bracket against, a dynamic ghost is extrapolated — clamped, and only for dynamic ghosts.

cards.title: Two pointers, one buffer
items: The write pointer moves when a packet lands, which is irregular
The read pointer moves with the client's own clock, a fixed depth behind
The gap between them is the entire jitter budget
Too shallow and you underrun and see a freeze; too deep and you added latency for nothing

cards.title: The depth is not just your setting
items: The configured window is two network ticks, which is a floor, not a ceiling
The measured arrival gap plus one and a quarter deviations competes with it
The larger of the two wins, clamped at six network intervals
So a lossy link silently deepens your buffer, and the delay you tuned is not the delay you get

cards.title: The read pointer never teleports for small errors
items: It corrects a tenth of the remaining error per frame
Its rate is clamped between 0.85 and 1.1 times normal
Only an error above ten ticks makes it snap outright
That is a phase-locked loop: slew the clock, do not step it

cards.title: It does extrapolate, and that surprises people
items: With no slot newer than the read pointer, a dynamic ghost runs the last known pair forward
The clamp is twenty simulation ticks by default, then it holds
A static ghost never extrapolates; it holds the last value instead
With exactly one slot in the buffer the factor is pinned to zero and nothing moves
